design_issues.screen: Claims detail — Attach Existing Form/Invoice selects
issues: React hydration console warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Caused by emergent editor instrumentation wrapping the dropdown option text ({f.title} · {f.patient_name}) with a <span> having style=display:contents inside <option>. Functionally the select works, but the console error is noisy. Consider using a plain string template inside <option> instead of a JSX expression that produces a span wrapper, or migrate to a shadcn Select if the visual freedom is desired.

action_items: (Low) Suppress the <span> in <option> hydration warning on Claims detail dropdowns (attach-form, attach-invoice).
critical_code_review_comments: claims.py `_invoice_pdf` uses latin-1 fallback (`_s`) which will silently mangle non-Latin characters in patient names / notes (e.g., ñ, accents common in the DR clinic context) — acceptable for now but consider switching to fpdf2 with a Unicode TTF font.

claims.py `delete_claim` does NOT delete underlying stored objects in object storage for uploaded/invoice PDFs — every deleted packet leaks its S3/storage blobs. Consider iterating `items[].storage_path` and calling storage.delete_object() before removing the packet.
claims.py `remove_item` also leaks the storage blob for the removed item (no delete_object call).

claims.py `upload_to_claim` file extension check runs on the client-provided filename only; no magic-byte / MIME sniff. Combined with the extension allowlist this is acceptable defense, but a PDF-disguised script uploaded as `.pdf` would be served with content-type application/pdf. Consider optional magic-byte validation for PDFs (%PDF-) as a defense-in-depth.
claims.py `merged_pdf` loads ALL items fully into memory then writes to another BytesIO — memory blow-up risk if a packet has many/large PDFs. Consider streaming or a hard cap on merged size.

Claims.js line 152 dropdown option text `{f.title} · {f.patient_name}` — the emergent instrumentation adds a <span> wrapper here which triggers hydration warning; a `title + ' · ' + patient_name` string concat would avoid the wrapper.

Claims.js `authedDownload` uses XMLHttpRequest via axios blob then constructs an <a>-click download. There is no `URL.revokeObjectURL` cleanup delay — some browsers may need setTimeout before revoke; consider a 100ms delay.

Claims.js does not confirm before delete (only relies on browser confirm from `remove`) — actually there is no confirm at all; delete fires instantly. Add a confirm() or shadcn AlertDialog to prevent accidental packet deletion.
